Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:10:1.hebrew: במקום עדים - דאנן סהדי דכל שעתא איכא מיא. וה"נ, כיון דאנן סהדי דכהנים חשודים על המומין — לא נימא "מה לי לשקר":
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:10:1.english: In a place of witnesses - For we are witnesses that there is always water [there]. And here too, since we are witnesses that priests are suspected regarding blemishes, we should not say, "Why would I lie?"

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:11:1.english: Here, he certainly cast a blemish in it - [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:11:2.english: This teaching - [The teaching] of Rabbi Ilai:

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:11:3.hebrew: בלא גברי - בסתמא אמר ליה: לא היו מוחזקין בו שהוא בכור כו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:11:3.english: Without [naming] a man - He stated it anonymously: “[If] it was not presumed to be a firstborn...” etc.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:12:1.english: Did we differentiate between a priest who is a ḥaver and a priest who is an am ha’aretz - And do we suspect me of intentionally inflicting a blemish upon it, like a priest who is an am ha’aretz?

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:12:2.english: Yes - We have differentiated, and you are not suspected.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:13:1.english: Masters of shields - [Meaning] shields. [These are] Torah scholars who battle in the war of Torah.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:15:1.english: How should I act - He could deny him.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:15:2.hebrew: אילמלי אני חי והוא מת - הייתי יכול להכחיש ולומר: "לא אמרתי":
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:15:2.english: If I were alive and he were dead - I would be able to deny [it] and say, "I did not say [this]."

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:15:3.hebrew: היאך יכול החי להכחיש את החי - ודאי כך אמרתי, וחוזרני בי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:15:3.english: How can the living contradict the living? - Certainly I said so, and I retract [it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:16:1.english: Stop, and he stopped - “Be silent,” and he was silent.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:17:1.hebrew: הראיתי בכור זה - לחכם, ואמר לי שמום קבוע הוא, ושוחטו; ובלבד שיהו לו עדים שלא הטילו בו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:17:1.english: I showed this firstborn - To a sage, and he told me that it is a permanent blemish; and he may slaughter it, provided that he has witnesses that they did not inflict [a blemish] upon it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:18:1.hebrew: נאמן הכהן לומר - לחכם: בכור זה נתן [לי] ישראל במום זה שבו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:18:1.english: A priest is deemed credible to say - To a sage: “An Israelite gave [me] this firstborn with this blemish that is on it.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:18:2.english: That is likely to be revealed - For the sage could come and say, "I did not permit it to you."

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:19:1.hebrew: לא, לעולם אימא לך: מילתא דעבידא לאיגלויי משקרי אינשי. והכא, היינו טעמא דמהימן: דלא חשידי כהני לאכול קדשים תמימים בחוץ; הלכך, אי לאו דשרי ליה חכם, לא הוה אמר שרא ליה ושחיט ליה בלא התרת מומחה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:19:1.english: No; actually, I could tell you that people [do] lie about a matter that is likely to be revealed. And here, this is the reason that he is believed: priests are not suspected of eating unblemished sacrificial meat outside [the Temple]; therefore, had a sage not permitted it to him, he would not say that [the sage] permitted it to him and slaughter it without the permission of an expert.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:19:2.hebrew: אבל הכא - דקא מחוי ליה לחכם, ואמר: "במום [זה] נתן לי ישראל", כדי שלא יצטרך להביא עדים שמאליו נפל בו — כיון דחשידי כהני להטיל מום ולמימר "נפל מאליו", חשידי נמי להטיל מום ולמימר: "ישראל נתנו לי במומו":
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:19:2.english: But here - Where [the priest] shows it to the sage and says, "An Israelite gave [it] to me with [this] blemish," so that he will not need to bring witnesses that it occurred on its own — since priests are suspected of inflicting a blemish and saying, "It occurred on its own," they are also suspected of inflicting a blemish and saying, "An Israelite gave it to me with its blemish."

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:1:1.hebrew: לאחזוקינהו - בחשודים, מי אמר? ר"מ "חשוד לדבר אחד, חשוד לכל התורה כולה" — היכא דמוחזק לן דעובר על דבר א':
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:1:1.english: To establish them - As suspects, did he say [this]? Rabbi Meir [maintains that] "one who is suspect regarding one matter is suspect regarding the entire Torah" [only] where it is established for us that he transgresses one matter.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:20:1.hebrew: קח לי ממי שהוא נאמן - שאינו לוקח פירות מעם הארץ, או ממי שלוקח מעם הארץ ומעשר דמאי קודם שימכרם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:20:1.english: Purchase for me from someone who is trusted - [One] who does not purchase produce from an am ha’aretz; or [the phrase “or from someone who tithes” means] from someone who purchases from an am ha’aretz and tithes [it as] demai before selling them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:20:2.english: [He is] not - This agent is [not] trusted to say: “I bought it from someone who is trusted.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:2:1.english: With regard to testimony of a firstborn - To testify that he did not intentionally inflict this blemish on it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:3:1.english: For testimony concerning a woman - That her husband died overseas.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:3:2.hebrew: תני אלא לעדות שאשה כשרה - ובעדות בכור נמי אשה כשרה, דאמרינן הלכתא כרבן שמעון, ואפי' בתו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:3:2.english: Teach: Only for testimony for which a woman is valid - And regarding the testimony of a firstborn [animal], a woman is also valid [to testify], as we say that the halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon, and even his daughter [is believed].

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:4:1.hebrew: יימר שרי בוכרא - יימר המתיר בכורות, לשון גנאי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:4:1.english: Yeimar permits firstborn [animals] - [Meaning,] “Yeimar who permits firstborns” — an expression of disparagement.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:5:1.hebrew: לא היו מוחזקין - בטלה שהוא בכור, ובא כהן בעליו ואמר: "בכור הוא זה, ומומו עמו" — שלא הוטל מום זה בכוונה — ואתי לאחוויי לחכם, אי קבוע הוא אי עובר הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:5:1.english: [People] did not presume - regarding a lamb that it is a firstborn, and the priest, its owner, came and said: "This is a firstborn, and its blemish is with it" — [meaning] that this blemish was not inflicted intentionally — and he comes to show [it] to a Sage [to determine] whether it is a permanent [blemish] or whether it is a transient [blemish]:

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:5:2.hebrew: נאמן - דהפה שאסר ואמר בכור הוא, התיר ואמר מומו עמו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:5:2.english: He is deemed credible - For the mouth that forbade and said, "It is a firstborn," [is the mouth that] permitted and said, "Its blemish is with it."

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:6:1.english: I was a married woman - And we never held a presumption regarding her that she was a married woman.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:6:2.english: She is deemed credible - And is permitted to marry.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:7:1.hebrew: דאי בעיא לא אמרה - כלומר, אי הוה חשידא להינשא בחיי בעלה בלא גירושין, הוה שתקה ולא אמרה "אשת איש הייתי", דהא בפנויה מחזקינן לה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:7:1.english: For if she wanted, she would not have said [anything] - That is to say, if she were suspected of marrying during her husband's lifetime without a divorce, she would have remained silent and not said, "I was a married woman," since we presume her to be an unmarried woman.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:7:2.hebrew: אבל הכא - בבכור, דלא סגיא דלא אמר "בכור הוא", דלימא ליה חכם מום קבוע הוא או עובר; דקדשים תמימים אין הכהן נחשד לאכול בחוץ — דבר כרת הוא — אבל נחשד להטיל בו מום, דלאו בעלמא הוא, ולא יהא נאמן — קמ"ל דנאמן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:7:2.english: But here - In [the case of] a firstborn, where it is not possible [for him] not to say, "It is a firstborn," so that a sage will tell him [whether] it is a permanent blemish or a transient one; for regarding unblemished sacrificial [animals], a priest is not suspected of eating [them] outside [the Temple courtyard] — [as] it is a matter of karet — but he is suspected of inflicting a blemish upon it, as [that] is merely an ordinary negative commandment, and [therefore] he should not be believed — [it] teaches us that he is believed.

Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:8:1.hebrew: דאם כן - דהוא הטיל בו מום, הוה שדי ביה מום הניכר אפי' לעם הארץ שהוא מום, ותו לא הוה בעי למיתי קמן ולמימר: ״בכור הוא״, דהא אין אדם אחר יודע שהוא בכור, ובקדשים בחוץ נמי ליכא לספוקיה, דהא מום ניכר שדא ביה. והיכא דאנן יודעין שהוא בכור, ליכא למימר הכי, דבעל כרחך אתי לקמן; דאי הוה שחיט ליה בלא מומחה, כיון דכולי עלמא ידעי שהוא בכור, הוו חשדי ליה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 36a:8:1.english: For if so - [That is to say,] that he inflicted a blemish upon it, he would have cast upon it a blemish that is recognizable even to an unlearned person as being a blemish, and furthermore he would not have needed to come before us and say, “It is a firstborn,” for no other person knows that it is a firstborn; nor is there [any reason] to suspect him of [eating] consecrated [meat] outside [the Temple courtyard], since he [would have] cast upon it a recognizable blemish. But where we [already] know that it is a firstborn, this cannot be said, for perforce he must come before us; for if he were to slaughter it without an expert, since everyone knows that it is a firstborn, they would suspect him.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:10:1.hebrew: ואמר רבא מה לו לשקר - רבה גרסינן, שהיה רבו של אביי, ולא רבא; דרבא אית ליה בהדיא בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף לג:) דמה לו לשקר במקום עדים לא אמרינן, דאמר: "דאביי ורבא לא סבירא להו הא דרב חסדא" כו':
Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:10:1.english: "And Rava said: Why would he lie" - We read [in the text] "Rabbah," who was the teacher of Abaye, and not "Rava"; for Rava explicitly holds in [the chapter entitled] Ḥezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 33b) that we do not say [the principle of] "Why would he lie" in a place where there are witnesses, as it states: "Abaye and Rava do not hold in accordance with this [statement] of Rav Ḥisda," etc.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:13:1.hebrew: בא לפני רבן גמליאל אמר ליה לאו - והלכה כן הוא, דאין חילוק בין חבר לעם הארץ; דבפרק בתרא דיומא (דף עח.), גבי ר' יוסי בן זימרא, דכהן הוה, ומיבעיא ליה: אי הלכה כר' מאיר, דאמר: "חשוד על הדבר לא דנו ולא מעידו", אי כרשב"ג, דאמר: "נאמן על של חבירו" — ש"מ דלרבי מאיר לא היה מתיר, אע"פ שהיה חבר:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:13:1.english: "He came before Rabban Gamliel; he said to him: No" - And the halakha is indeed so, that there is no distinction between a ḥaver and an am ha’aretz. For in the last chapter of Yoma (78a), regarding Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra, who was a priest, and he raised the dilemma whether the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who said: "One who is suspected of a matter may neither judge it nor testify about it," or in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who said: "He is believed regarding [the property] of his fellow" — learn from this that according to Rabbi Meir, he could not permit [firstborn animals], even though he was a ḥaver.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:14:1.hebrew: עמד השואל ושאל - בפ' נערה בנדרים בירושלמי דריש, מדכתיב: "ועמדו שני האנשים" בוי"ו — דשואל הלכות ואגדות צריך לעמוד:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:14:1.english: The questioner stood and asked - In the chapter [entitled] Na'arah in Nedarim in the Yerushalmi, it expounds from that which is written: "And the two men shall stand" with a vav, that one who inquires about halakhot and aggadot must stand.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:15:1.hebrew: עמוד על רגליך ויעידו בך - לא גרסי' "ויעידו בך", לא כאן ולא בפרק תפלת השחר ברישיה (ברכות כז:) — דמה עדות שייך כאן? אלא בסנהדרין בריש פרק כהן גדול (סנהדרין דף יט.) גרסינן ליה, גבי עובדא דינאי; ואגב פשטא דהתם נכתב כאן:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:15:1.english: "Stand on your feet and they will testify against you" - We do not read "and they will testify against you," neither here nor at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Tefillat HaShachar (Berakhot 27b), for what testimony is relevant here? Rather, in Sanhedrin at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Kohen Gadol (Sanhedrin 19a) we read it, regarding the incident of Yannai; and due to the routine flow of [the text] there, it was written here.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:15:2.hebrew: היאך החי יכול להכחיש החי - כלומר: סבור הייתי להעלים, ואיני יכול. ובקונט' פירש: דודאי כך אמרתי, וחזרתי בי. וא"א כן, דבפרק תפלת השחר (ברכות דף כז:) פסק שם הלכה כמותו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:15:2.english: "How can the living contradict the living" - That is to say: I had thought to conceal [it], but I am unable [to do so]. And in the Kuntres [Rashi] explained: "Certainly I said so, and I retract." Yet it is impossible [to say] so, for in the chapter [entitled] Tefillat HaShachar (Berakhot 27b), [the Gemara] ruled there that the halakhah is in accordance with his opinion.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:16:1.english: Rabbi Ḥutzpit the disseminator - [He was] one of the Ten Martyrs of the monarchy.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:1:1.hebrew: אימר דא"ר מאיר לחששא כו' - מתוך הלשון משמע דאליבא דר' מאיר קאמר, ולא סבירא לן כוותיה, אלא אפילו במוחזק עובר על דבר א' לא הוי חשוד על כל התורה כולה. ואע"ג דבפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כז.) אמר אביי: "עבריין אוכל נבילות להכעיס פסול לעדות", ומוקים לה כרבי מאיר, וקיימא לן כוותיה דהוא מיע"ל קג"ם — היינו דוקא לענין עדות, דרחמנא אמר: "אל תשת רשע עד", אבל בשאר מילי לא חשיד. ומיהו, ר' מאיר דקאמר התם: "עד זומם פסול לכל התורה כולה" — ה"נ הוה מצי למינקט אחד משאר דברים, ולא נקט עד זומם אלא לאפוקי מדר' יוסי, דאפילו עד זומם נמי מכשר לדיני נפשות כשהוזם בדיני ממונות:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 36a:1:1.english: Say that Rabbi Meir says [this] as a concern, etc. - From the wording, it is implied that [the Gemara] is speaking according to [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir, and we do not hold in accordance with him; rather, even [one who is] established as transgressing one matter is not suspected regarding the entire Torah. And even though in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 27a), Abaye said: "A transgressor who eats carcasses [neveilot] out of spite is disqualified from [giving] testimony," and he establishes it according to Rabbi Meir, and we hold in accordance with him because it is [one of the cases of] YA'AL KAGAM — that is specifically regarding testimony, for the Merciful One states: "Do not place a wicked person as a witness" (Exodus 23:1); but regarding other matters, he is not suspected. However, [as for] Rabbi Meir, who said there: "A scheming witness is disqualified for the entire Torah" — he could also have cited one of the other matters, and he cited a scheming witness only to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Yose, who declares even a scheming witness valid for capital cases when he was found scheming in monetary cases.
